title.zh: 卷251 列傳三十八 图海 李之芳
title.en: Volume 251 Biographies 38: Tu Hai, Li Zhifang
title.raw: 卷251 列傳三十八 图海 李之芳

sentences.zh: 列傳三十八

translations.literal: Biographies 38
translations.idiomatic: Biographies 38

sentences.zh: 圖海李之芳圖海，字麟洲，馬佳氏，滿洲正黃旗人。

translations.literal: Tu Hai and Li Zhifang. Tu Hai, styled Linzhou, of the Majia clan, was a Manchu of the Plain Yellow Banner.
translations.idiomatic: Tu Hai and Li Zhifang. Tu Hai, whose style was Linzhou, belonged to the Majia clan and was a Manchu of the Plain Yellow Banner.

sentences.zh: 父穆哈達，世居綏芬。

translations.literal: His father Muha'da had long resided in Suifen.
translations.idiomatic: His father Muha'da came from a family that had long lived in Suifen.

sentences.zh: 圖海自筆帖式歷國史院侍讀。

translations.literal: Tu Hai rose from copy clerk to reader in the Grand Secretariat of National History.
translations.idiomatic: Tu Hai worked his way up from copy clerk to reader at the Grand Secretariat of National History.

sentences.zh: 世祖嘗幸南苑，負寶從，顧其舉止，以為非常人。

translations.literal: The Shizu Emperor once visited the Southern Park; Tu Hai carried the imperial seal in attendance, and the emperor observed his bearing and regarded him as no ordinary man.
translations.idiomatic: When the Shizu Emperor once visited the Southern Park, Tu Hai attended carrying the imperial seal. The emperor took note of his bearing and judged him a man of uncommon ability.

sentences.zh: 擢內秘書院學士，授拜他喇布勒哈番，遷弘文院大學士、議政大臣。

translations.literal: He was promoted to academician of the Inner Secretariat, granted the rank of Defender of the Nation Baturu, and transferred to Grand Secretary of the Hall of Literary Glory and minister of state deliberation.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to academician of the Inner Secretariat, granted the Defender of the Nation Baturu rank, and then made Grand Secretary of the Hall of Literary Glory and a deliberating minister of state.

sentences.zh: 順治十二年，加太子太保，攝刑部尚書事。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year of Shunzhi he was given the additional title Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent and acted as Minister of Justice.
translations.idiomatic: In Shunzhi 12 he received the additional title Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent and served concurrently as Minister of Justice.

sentences.zh: 與大學士巴哈納等同訂律例。

translations.literal: Together with Grand Secretary Bahana and others he revised the legal code.
translations.idiomatic: He worked with Grand Secretary Bahana and others to compile the revised legal code.

sentences.zh: 侍衛阿拉那與公額爾克戴青兩家奴鬥於市，讞失實，坐欺罔，免死，削職。

translations.literal: When the bodyguard Alana and the bond-servants of the duke Erke Daiqing fought in the market, his judgment did not match the facts; he was convicted of deception, spared death, and stripped of office.
translations.idiomatic: When a bodyguard named Alana and the bond-servants of Duke Erke Daiqing fought in the market, Tu Hai's ruling did not square with the facts. Convicted of deceiving the court, he was spared execution but dismissed from office.

sentences.zh: 世祖崩，遺命起用。

translations.literal: When the Shizu Emperor died, his testamentary edict ordered Tu Hai reinstated.
translations.idiomatic: On the Shizu Emperor's death, his final edict ordered Tu Hai brought back into service.

sentences.zh: 聖祖即位，授正黃旗滿洲都統。

translations.literal: When the Sacred Ancestor took the throne, Tu Hai was appointed banner general of the Manchu Plain Yellow Banner.
translations.idiomatic: After the Kangxi Emperor ascended the throne, Tu Hai was made banner general of the Manchu Plain Yellow Banner.

sentences.zh: 李自成餘眾郝搖旗、劉體純、李來亨嘯聚鄖、襄間。

translations.literal: The remnant followers of Li Zicheng—Hao Yaoqi, Liu Tichun, and Li Laiheng—rallied between Yun and Xiang.
translations.idiomatic: Remnants of Li Zicheng's forces—Hao Yaoqi, Liu Tichun, and Li Laiheng—gathered and held out between Yun and Xiang.

sentences.zh: 康熙二年，命圖海為定西將軍，副靖西將軍都統穆里瑪，將禁旅，會湖廣、四川諸軍討之，屢破賊。

translations.literal: In the second year of Kangxi he was ordered to serve as Pacifier of the West General, assisting Pacifier of the West General and banner commander Murima, leading the imperial guard and joining the armies of Huguang and Sichuan to suppress them, repeatedly defeating the rebels.
translations.idiomatic: In Kangxi 2 Tu Hai was appointed Pacifier of the West General, second to banner commander Murima, Pacifier of the West. He led the imperial guard, joined forces from Huguang and Sichuan, and repeatedly routed the rebels.

sentences.zh: 未幾，郝搖旗為副都統杜敏所擒，劉體純亦破滅，惟李來亨據茅麓山，恃險負固，圖海圍之，絕其外援。

translations.literal: Before long Hao Yaoqi was captured by Vice Banner Commander Du Min, Liu Tichun was also destroyed, and only Li Laiheng held Maolu Mountain, relying on its terrain and stubbornly resisting; Tu Hai besieged him and cut off outside aid.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Hao Yaoqi was taken by Vice Banner Commander Du Min and Liu Tichun's force was wiped out. Only Li Laiheng remained on Maolu Mountain, holding the heights in a last stand. Tu Hai besieged him and severed his outside support.

sentences.zh: 來亨窮蹙，自焚死，其下以眾降。

translations.literal: Laiheng, driven to extremity, burned himself to death, and his followers surrendered with their whole force.
translations.idiomatic: Cornered, Laiheng set himself on fire and died; his followers surrendered en masse.

sentences.zh: 執斬明新樂王及所署置官屬，俘三千餘以還。

translations.literal: He seized and executed the Ming Prince of Xinle and the officials Li had appointed, and returned with more than three thousand captives.
translations.idiomatic: He captured and executed the Ming Prince of Xinle along with Li's appointed officials, then returned with more than three thousand prisoners.

sentences.zh: 六年，復為弘文院大學士，進一等阿達哈哈番。

translations.literal: In the sixth year he again became Grand Secretary of the Hall of Literary Glory and was advanced to first-class Ada Ha Banner rank.
translations.idiomatic: In Kangxi 6 he was again made Grand Secretary of the Hall of Literary Glory and promoted to first-class Ada Ha Banner rank.

sentences.zh: 頃之，以兼都統乞解機務，不許。

translations.literal: Shortly afterward, citing his concurrent post as banner general, he begged to be relieved of state affairs; the request was denied.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward he asked to be relieved of ministerial duties on account of his concurrent banner command; the court refused.

sentences.zh: 九年，改中和殿大學士，兼禮部尚書。

translations.literal: In the ninth year he was changed to Grand Secretary of the Hall of Central Harmony and concurrently served as Minister of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: In Kangxi 9 he became Grand Secretary of the Hall of Central Harmony and concurrently Minister of Rites.

sentences.zh: 十二年，平南王尚可喜請老。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year the Pacifier of the South Prince Shang Kexi asked to retire.
translations.idiomatic: In Kangxi 12 the Pacifier of the South, Prince Shang Kexi, petitioned to retire.

sentences.zh: 七月，吳三桂繼之，實探朝旨。

translations.literal: In the seventh month Wu Sangui followed suit, in fact to probe the court's intent.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month Wu Sangui did the same—chiefly to sound out the court's intentions.

sentences.zh: 廷議移籓狀，莫洛、米思翰、明珠等皆主如所請，惟圖海持不可。

translations.literal: At court the question of removing the princely fiefs was debated; Moluo, Misihan, Mingzhu, and others all favored granting the requests, but only Tu Hai held that it should not be done.
translations.idiomatic: When the court debated removing the princely fiefs, Moluo, Misihan, Mingzhu, and others all favored acceding to the requests—only Tu Hai opposed it.

sentences.zh: 上意決，遂黜圖海議。

translations.literal: The emperor's mind was set, and Tu Hai's view was accordingly set aside.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor had already made up his mind, and Tu Hai's dissent was set aside.

sentences.zh: 三桂既反，命攝戶部，理餉運。

translations.literal: After Sangui rebelled, Tu Hai was ordered to act as head of the Ministry of Revenue and manage supply transport.
translations.idiomatic: Once Sangui had risen in revolt, Tu Hai was put in charge of the Ministry of Revenue to manage grain and supply transport.

sentences.zh: 十四年，察哈爾布爾尼劫其父阿布柰以叛。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year the Chahar Bulwendi seized his father Abunai and rebelled.
translations.idiomatic: In Kangxi 14 the Chahar prince Bulwendi took his father Abunai hostage and rebelled.

sentences.zh: 命信郡王鄂扎為撫遠大將軍，圖海副之，討布爾尼。

translations.literal: The Trustful Prince Ezha was appointed Pacifying the Distant Grand General with Tu Hai as his deputy to campaign against Bulwendi.
translations.idiomatic: Trustful Prince Ezha was named Pacifying the Distant Grand General, with Tu Hai as deputy, to suppress Bulwendi.

sentences.zh: 時禁旅多調發，圖海請籍八旗家奴驍健者率以行，在路騷掠，一不問。

translations.literal: As the imperial guard had largely been deployed, Tu Hai requested that stalwart bond-servants of the Eight Banners be registered and led on campaign; they plundered along the road, and he did not inquire into a single case.
translations.idiomatic: With most of the imperial guard already deployed, Tu Hai had sturdy banner bond-servants mustered to march with the army. They looted along the route, and he ignored every complaint.

sentences.zh: 至，下令曰：「察哈爾元裔，多珍寶，破之富且倍！

translations.literal: On arrival he issued an order: "The Chahar are Yuan descendants and hold many treasures; defeat them and your wealth will more than double!"
translations.idiomatic: On reaching the front he proclaimed: "The Chahar are descendants of the Yuan and sit on great treasure—break them and you will be more than twice as rich!"

sentences.zh: 」於是士卒奮勇，無不一當百。

translations.literal: Thereupon the troops fought with spirit, each man worth a hundred.
translations.idiomatic: The men took heart, and each fought as if he were worth a hundred.

sentences.zh: 戰於達祿，布爾尼設伏山谷，別以三千人來拒。

translations.literal: They fought at Dalu; Bulwendi set an ambush in the valleys and separately sent three thousand men to resist.
translations.idiomatic: At Dalu, Bulwendi laid an ambush in the valleys and sent another three thousand men to block the advance.

sentences.zh: 既戰，伏發，土默特兵挫。

translations.literal: Once battle was joined the ambush struck and the Tumed troops were checked.
translations.idiomatic: When battle was joined the ambush sprang, and the Tumed contingent was thrown into disorder.

sentences.zh: 圖海分兵迎擊，敵以四百騎繼進，力戰，覆其眾。

translations.literal: Tu Hai divided his force to meet the attack; the enemy sent four hundred horsemen in support, fought fiercely, and was overrun.
translations.idiomatic: Tu Hai split off a detachment to counterattack; when four hundred enemy horsemen came up in support, his men fought hard and annihilated them.

sentences.zh: 布爾尼乃悉眾出，用火攻，圖海令嚴陣待，連擊大破之，招撫人戶一千三百餘。

translations.literal: Bulwendi then brought out his entire force and used fire attack; Tu Hai ordered strict formation and waiting, struck repeatedly and routed them utterly, and brought over more than thirteen hundred households.
translations.idiomatic: Bulwendi then committed his whole army and used fire attacks. Tu Hai held a tight formation, counterattacked again and again, and broke them completely, winning over more than thirteen hundred households.

sentences.zh: 布爾尼以三十騎遁，科爾沁額駙沙津追斬之，察哈爾平。

translations.literal: Bulwendi fled with thirty horsemen; the Khorchin imperial son-in-law Shajin pursued and killed him, and the Chahar were pacified.
translations.idiomatic: Bulwendi escaped with thirty riders; Khorchin imperial son-in-law Shajin ran him down and killed him, and the Chahar were pacified.

sentences.zh: 師還，聖祖禦南苑大紅門，行郊勞禮。

translations.literal: When the army returned, the Sacred Ancestor proceeded to the Great Red Gate of the Southern Park and performed the suburban ceremony of welcoming the troops.
translations.idiomatic: On the army's return the Kangxi Emperor went to the Great Red Gate of the Southern Park to perform the suburban welcome for the victorious troops.

sentences.zh: 敘功，進一等阿思哈尼哈番。

translations.literal: His merit was recorded and he was advanced to first-class Asihani Banner rank.
translations.idiomatic: His services were rewarded with promotion to first-class Asihani Banner rank.

sentences.zh: 陝西提督王輔臣以平涼叛應三桂，定西大將軍貝勒董額督諸軍攻之，久未下。

translations.literal: Shaanxi Provincial Commander Wang Fuchen rebelled at Pingliang in support of Sangui; the Pacifier of the West Grand General, Prince Dong'e, directed the armies against him, but the city was long not taken.
translations.idiomatic: Shaanxi Provincial Commander Wang Fuchen rebelled at Pingliang in league with Sangui. Pacifier of the West Grand General Prince Dong'e led the siege, yet the city held out for a long time.

sentences.zh: 三桂遣王屏籓、吳之茂等犯秦、隴，欲與平涼合。

translations.literal: Sangui sent Wang Pingfan, Wu Zhimao, and others to invade Qin and Long, intending to join forces with Pingliang.
translations.idiomatic: Sangui sent Wang Pingfan, Wu Zhimao, and others into Qin and Long, aiming to link up with the Pingliang garrison.

sentences.zh: 十五年，以圖海為撫遠大將軍，八旗每佐領出護軍二名，率以往。

translations.literal: In the fifteenth year Tu Hai was made Pacifying the Distant Grand General; each company of the Eight Banners furnished two guardsmen, and he led them on campaign.
translations.idiomatic: In Kangxi 15 Tu Hai was appointed Pacifying the Distant Grand General. Each banner company supplied two guardsmen, and he marched west at their head.

sentences.zh: 臨發，上御太和殿賜敕印，命諸軍咸聽節制。

translations.literal: On the eve of departure the emperor proceeded to the Hall of Supreme Harmony, bestowed the command seal and edict, and ordered all armies to obey his direction.
translations.idiomatic: Before he set out, the emperor received him in the Hall of Supreme Harmony, gave him the command seal and edict, and placed every army under his orders.

sentences.zh: 既至，明賞罰，申約束。

translations.literal: After he arrived he made rewards and punishments clear and enforced discipline.
translations.idiomatic: Once on the ground he made rewards and punishments unmistakable and tightened discipline throughout the command.

sentences.zh: 諸將請乘勢攻城，圖海宣言曰：「仁義之師，先招撫，後攻伐。

translations.literal: The generals asked to press the assault on the city; Tu Hai proclaimed: "An army of benevolence and righteousness first offers surrender, then attacks."
translations.idiomatic: When his generals urged an immediate assault, Tu Hai declared: "A humane army wins men over before it strikes."

sentences.zh: 今奉天威討叛豎，無慮不克。

translations.literal: Now, bearing Heaven's majesty to punish rebels, there is no doubt of victory.
translations.idiomatic: We march under Heaven's mandate to crush these rebels—victory is certain.

sentences.zh: 顧城中生靈數十萬，覆巢之下，殺戮必多。

translations.literal: Yet within the city are hundreds of thousands of lives; when the nest is overturned, slaughter will surely be great.
translations.idiomatic: Yet hundreds of thousands of lives are trapped inside; when the nest is torn apart, the killing will be immense.

sentences.zh: 當體聖主好生之德，俟其向化。

translations.literal: We should embody the Sacred Lord's virtue of cherishing life and wait for them to turn to allegiance.
translations.idiomatic: We must honor the emperor's love of life and give them time to submit of their own accord.

sentences.zh: 」城中聞者，莫不感泣，思自拔。

translations.literal: Those within the city who heard this were moved to tears and thought of extricating themselves.
translations.idiomatic: Word spread inside the walls; men wept and began to think of breaking away from the rebels.

sentences.zh: 五月，奪虎山墩，虎山墩者，在平涼城北，高數十仞，賊守以精兵，通餉道。

translations.literal: In the fifth month he seized Tiger Hill Redoubt; Tiger Hill Redoubt stood north of Pingliang city, rose several tens of ren in height, was held by elite rebel troops, and controlled the supply route.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month he took Tiger Hill Redoubt north of Pingliang—a height of many tens of ren held by elite rebels and the lifeline of their grain road.

sentences.zh: 圖海曰：「此平涼咽喉也。

translations.literal: Tu Hai said: "This is the throat of Pingliang."
translations.idiomatic: Tu Hai said, "This is Pingliang's throat."

sentences.zh: 」率兵仰攻，賊萬餘列火器以拒師。

translations.literal: He led troops in an uphill assault; more than ten thousand rebels lined firearms to resist the army.
translations.idiomatic: He led his men up the slope; more than ten thousand defenders massed firearms to block them.

sentences.zh: 圖海令兵更迭進，自巳至午，戰益力，遂奪而據之，發大砲攻城，城人洶懼。

translations.literal: Tu Hai ordered the troops to advance in relays from the si hour to the wu hour, fighting with growing force until they seized and held it, then opened great cannon on the city, and the inhabitants were thrown into panic.
translations.idiomatic: Tu Hai sent his men forward in relays from mid-morning to noon, pressing harder until the redoubt fell. He then turned heavy guns on the city, and panic spread among its people.

sentences.zh: 圖海用幕客周昌策，招輔臣降。

translations.literal: Tu Hai employed the stratagem of his secretary Zhou Chang to induce Fuchen to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: Tu Hai followed a plan devised by his secretary Zhou Chang to bring Fuchen over.

sentences.zh: 昌，字培公，荊門諸生。

translations.literal: Chang, styled Peigong, was a licentiate of Jingmen.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou Chang, style Peigong, was a licentiate from Jingmen.

sentences.zh: 好奇計。

translations.literal: He delighted in ingenious stratagems.
translations.idiomatic: He was fond of bold stratagems.

sentences.zh: 佐振武將軍吳丹有勞，以七品官錄用。

translations.literal: He assisted Pacifier of Martial Valor General Wu Dan with merit and was enrolled as a seventh-rank official.
translations.idiomatic: After serving Pacifier of Martial Valor Wu Dan with distinction, he was enrolled as a seventh-rank official.

sentences.zh: 圖海次潼關，以策乾之，客諸幕。

translations.literal: When Tu Hai halted at Tong Pass he was impressed by Chang's plans and kept him in his secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: When Tu Hai camped at Tong Pass he took to Chang's plans and brought him onto his staff.

sentences.zh: 輔臣所署置總兵黃九疇、布政使龔榮遇皆昌鄉人，屢勸輔臣反正，以蠟丸告昌，昌白圖海。

translations.literal: Fuchen's appointed regional commander Huang Jiuchou and provincial administration commissioner Gong Rongyu were both fellow townsmen of Chang; they repeatedly urged Fuchen to return to allegiance, sent word to Chang in wax pellets, and Chang informed Tu Hai.
translations.idiomatic: Regional commander Huang Jiuchou and administration commissioner Gong Rongyu, whom Fuchen had appointed, were both from Chang's home district. They kept urging Fuchen to return to the throne, sent messages to Chang in wax pellets, and Chang reported this to Tu Hai.

sentences.zh: 圖海即令昌入城諭降，輔臣遣其將從昌出謁，圖海聞上，上許之。

translations.literal: Tu Hai at once ordered Chang into the city to urge surrender; Fuchen sent a general out with Chang to pay respects; Tu Hai reported to the throne, and the emperor approved.
translations.idiomatic: Tu Hai sent Chang into the city to negotiate surrender. Fuchen dispatched a general with him to pay respects outside the walls. Tu Hai reported to the throne, and the emperor consented.

sentences.zh: 乃假昌參議道，賚詔往撫。

translations.literal: He then lent Chang the title of participation commissioner and sent him with an imperial edict to pacify the city.
translations.idiomatic: Chang was given the acting rank of participation commissioner and sent in with an imperial edict to win them over.

sentences.zh: 輔臣使榮遇上軍民冊，子繼貞繳三桂所授敕印，顧猶觀望，復命昌偕兄子保定諭之，乃薙發降。

translations.literal: Fuchen had Rongyu present the register of troops and civilians; his son Jizhen surrendered the seal and edict Sangui had granted; yet he still hesitated, so Chang was again sent with his nephew Baoding to persuade him, and only then did he shave his head and surrender.
translations.idiomatic: Fuchen had Rongyu submit the civilian and military rolls; his son Jizhen handed over the seal and patent Wu Sangui had given him. Still Fuchen wavered, until Chang went in again with his nephew Baoding to persuade him; then he shaved his head and submitted.

sentences.zh: 因令吳丹入城撫定。

translations.literal: Tu Hai then ordered Wu Dan to enter the city and pacify it.
translations.idiomatic: Tu Hai then sent Wu Dan into the city to restore order.

sentences.zh: 吳之茂聞平涼下，自秦州遁，遣將軍佛尼勒敗之於牡丹園，又敗之於西和縣北山。

translations.literal: When Wu Zhimao heard that Pingliang had fallen he fled from Qinzhou; General Fonile was sent and defeated him at Mudan Garden and again on North Mountain in Xihe County.
translations.idiomatic: Hearing that Pingliang had fallen, Wu Zhimao fled from Qinzhou. General Fonile routed him at Mudan Garden and again on North Mountain in Xihe County.

sentences.zh: 將軍穆佔進攻王屏籓於樂門，敗賊於紅崖，復禮縣。

translations.literal: General Muzhan advanced against Wang Pingfan at Lemen, defeated the rebels at Red Cliff, and recovered Li County.
translations.idiomatic: General Muzhan pressed Wang Pingfan at Lemen, broke the rebels at Red Cliff, and recovered Li County.

sentences.zh: 輔臣所署置巡撫陳彭，總兵週養民、王好問等相繼降。

translations.literal: Fuchen's appointed provincial governor Chen Peng, regional commanders Zhou Yangmin, Wang Haowen, and others surrendered one after another.
translations.idiomatic: Provincial governor Chen Peng and regional commanders Zhou Yangmin and Wang Haowen, whom Fuchen had appointed, surrendered in turn.

sentences.zh: 秦地略定。

translations.literal: The Qin region was largely pacified.
translations.idiomatic: The Qin region was largely brought under control.

sentences.zh: 敘功，進三等公，世襲。

translations.literal: His merit was recorded and he was advanced to third-rank duke with hereditary succession.
translations.idiomatic: For his services he was made a third-rank duke with a hereditary title.

sentences.zh: 圖海疏請遣兵赴湖廣，會徵三桂，上命圖海親率精銳以行。

translations.literal: Tu Hai memorialized asking to send troops to Huguang to join the campaign against Sangui; the emperor ordered Tu Hai personally to lead elite troops thither.
translations.idiomatic: Tu Hai asked to send forces to Huguang to join the campaign against Sangui; the emperor ordered him to lead the elite corps in person.

sentences.zh: 圖海疏陳陝西初定、反側未安狀，乃授穆佔征南將軍，率滿洲兵及平涼降卒往，圖海仍留鎮。

translations.literal: Tu Hai memorialized that Shaanxi had only just been pacified and disaffection was not yet settled; Muzhan was then made Pacifier of the South General to lead Manchu troops and Pingliang surrendered soldiers thither, while Tu Hai remained to garrison the region.
translations.idiomatic: Tu Hai explained that Shaanxi had only just been secured and loyalties were still unsettled. Muzhan was made Pacifier of the South and sent south with Manchu troops and Pingliang defectors, while Tu Hai stayed behind to hold the province.

sentences.zh: 時平涼、慶陽雖下，漢中、興安猶為賊據。

translations.literal: At that time although Pingliang and Qingyang had fallen, Hanzhong and Xing'an were still held by rebels.
translations.idiomatic: Pingliang and Qingyang were in hand, but Hanzhong and Xing'an remained in rebel hands.

sentences.zh: 圖海奏調綠旗兵，期明年正月檄提督孫思克赴秦州，趙良棟赴鳳翔，與張勇、王進寶會師進取，勇等謂須俟夏秋。

translations.literal: Tu Hai memorialized to transfer Green Standard troops, planning that in the first month of the coming year Provincial Commander Sun Sike would be ordered to Qinzhou and Zhao Liangdong to Fengxiang to join Zhang Yong and Wang Jinbao in a converging advance; Yong and others said they must wait until summer and autumn.
translations.idiomatic: Tu Hai asked for Green Standard reinforcements and planned to order Sun Sike to Qinzhou and Zhao Liangdong to Fengxiang in the first month of the new year, there to join Zhang Yong and Wang Jinbao for a joint advance. Yong and the others insisted they must wait until summer or autumn.

sentences.zh: 上慮克漢中、興安轉餉難，令守諸要隘，分兵赴荊州攻三桂。

translations.literal: The emperor feared that taking Hanzhong and Xing'an would make supply transport difficult, ordered the garrison of key passes, and sent detachments to Jingzhou to attack Sangui.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor worried that seizing Hanzhong and Xing'an would strain supply lines, so he ordered the key passes held and detachments sent to Jingzhou against Sangui.

sentences.zh: 十六年，圖海招撫韓城等縣偽官，又遣兵逼禮縣、益門，先後敗賊五盤山、喬家山、塘坊廟、芭蕉園、沙窩諸處，复塔什堡。

translations.literal: In the sixteenth year Tu Hai won over the false officials of Hancheng and other counties, also sent troops to press Li County and Yimen, and in succession defeated rebels at Wupanshan, Qiaojiashan, Tangfangmiao, Bajiaoyuan, Shawo, and other places, recovering Tashibao.
translations.idiomatic: In Kangxi 16 Tu Hai induced the puppet officials of Hancheng and neighboring counties to submit, pressed Li County and Yimen, and in a series of actions routed rebel bands at Wupanshan, Qiaojiashan, Tangfang Temple, Bajiao Garden, Shawo, and elsewhere, retaking Tashibao.

sentences.zh: 十七年，复疏請分兵下漢中、興安，上密諭止之。

translations.literal: In the seventeenth year he again memorialized asking to divide forces and descend on Hanzhong and Xing'an; the emperor secretly instructed him to stop.
translations.idiomatic: In Kangxi 17 he again asked to split forces and take Hanzhong and Xing'an; the emperor privately told him to hold off.

sentences.zh: 將軍佛尼勒等又敗賊牛頭山香泉，四川總督周有德亦敗賊秦嶺，复潼關堡五寨。

translations.literal: General Fonile and others again defeated rebels at Niutoushan Xiangquan; Sichuan Governor-General Zhou Youde also defeated rebels on the Qin Mountains and recovered the five stockades of Tongguan Fort.
translations.idiomatic: General Fonile routed the rebels again at Niutoushan Xiangquan, while Sichuan Governor-General Zhou Youde beat them on the Qin Mountains and retook the five stockades of Tongguan Fort.

sentences.zh: 慶陽賊袁本秀受三桂劄，謀亂。

translations.literal: The Qingyang rebel Yuan Benxiu received a dispatch from Sangui and plotted disorder.
translations.idiomatic: At Qingyang the rebel Yuan Benxiu, having received orders from Sangui, plotted an uprising.

sentences.zh: 圖海發慶陽、宜君、延安三營兵，會王進寶討平之，斬本秀衛遠溝。

translations.literal: Tu Hai sent troops from the three camps of Qingyang, Yijun, and Yan'an, joined Wang Jinbao to suppress them, and beheaded Benxiu at Weiyuangou.
translations.idiomatic: Tu Hai sent the Qingyang, Yijun, and Yan'an garrisons, joined Wang Jinbao to crush the plot, and beheaded Benxiu at Weiyuangou.

sentences.zh: 頃之，入覲。

translations.literal: Shortly afterward he entered court audience.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he went to court for an audience.

sentences.zh: 十八年，還鎮。

translations.literal: In the eighteenth year he returned to his command.
translations.idiomatic: In Kangxi 18 he returned to his post.

sentences.zh: 湖南、廣西平。

translations.literal: Hunan and Guangxi were pacified.
translations.idiomatic: Hunan and Guangxi were pacified.

sentences.zh: 上命亟攻寶雞，規取漢中、興安，定四川。

translations.literal: The emperor ordered a swift attack on Baoji, planning to take Hanzhong and Xing'an and settle Sichuan.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ordered an immediate drive on Baoji, aiming to seize Hanzhong and Xing'an and secure Sichuan.

sentences.zh: 圖海乃厲師攻益門鎮，破之。

translations.literal: Tu Hai then stiffened the army's discipline and attacked Yimen Town, breaking it.
translations.idiomatic: Tu Hai tightened discipline and stormed Yimen Town, taking it.

sentences.zh: 會賊毀偏橋，兵不得進，狀聞，詔嚴責。

translations.literal: But the rebels destroyed the Pian Bridge and the troops could not advance; the report reached the throne and an edict sternly rebuked him.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels destroyed Pian Bridge and blocked the advance. When word reached Beijing, an edict rebuked him sharply.

sentences.zh: 乃決策期分四路：圖海親率將軍佛尼勒等趨興安，總兵官程福亮為後援，屯舊縣關；

translations.literal: He then resolved on a timed advance in four columns: Tu Hai personally would lead General Fonile and others toward Xing'an, Regional Commander Cheng Fuliang as rear support stationed at Jiuxian Pass;
translations.idiomatic: He then set a coordinated advance on four axes: Tu Hai would lead General Fonile and others toward Xing'an, with Regional Commander Cheng Fuliang in reserve at Jiuxian Pass;

sentences.zh: 將軍畢力克圖、提督孫思克等自略陽進，總兵官硃衣客為後援，駐西河；

translations.literal: General Biliketu and Provincial Commander Sun Sike and others would advance from Lueyang, Regional Commander Zhu Yike as rear support stationed at Xihe;
translations.idiomatic: General Biliketu and Provincial Commander Sun Sike would advance from Lueyang, with Regional Commander Zhu Yike in reserve at Xihe;

sentences.zh: 將軍王進寶、總兵官費雅達自棧道進，總兵官高孟為後援，駐寶雞；

translations.literal: General Wang Jinbao and Regional Commander Feiyada would advance by the plank road, Regional Commander Gao Meng as rear support stationed at Baoji;
translations.idiomatic: General Wang Jinbao and Regional Commander Feiyada would move up the plank road, with Regional Commander Gao Meng holding Baoji in reserve;

sentences.zh: 提督趙良棟自徽縣進。

translations.literal: Provincial Commander Zhao Liangdong would advance from Huixian.
translations.idiomatic: Provincial Commander Zhao Liangdong would advance from Huixian.

sentences.zh: 十月，師次鎮安，分兵為二隊，進敗三桂將王遇隆，渡乾玉河，奪梁河關。

translations.literal: In the tenth month the army halted at Zhen'an, divided into two columns, advanced and defeated Sangui's general Wang Yulong, crossed the Qianyu River, and seized Lianghe Pass.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month the army reached Zhen'an, split into two columns, routed Sangui's general Wang Yulong, crossed the Qianyu River, and took Lianghe Pass.

sentences.zh: 三桂將韓晉卿遁。

translations.literal: Sangui's general Han Jinqing fled.
translations.idiomatic: Sangui's general Han Jinqing fled.

sentences.zh: 進寶亦復漢中。

translations.literal: Jinbao also recovered Hanzhong.
translations.idiomatic: Jinbao recovered Hanzhong as well.

sentences.zh: 良棟复徽縣、略陽。

translations.literal: Liangdong recovered Huixian and Lueyang.
translations.idiomatic: Liangdong retook Huixian and Lueyang.

sentences.zh: 畢力克圖復成縣，又復階州，遣參將康調元復文縣。

translations.literal: Biliketu recovered Cheng County, then Jiezhou, and sent Assistant Regional Commander Kang Tiaoyuan to recover Wen County.
translations.idiomatic: Biliketu retook Cheng County and Jiezhou, and sent Assistant Regional Commander Kang Tiaoyuan to recover Wen County.

sentences.zh: 於是平利、紫陽、石泉、漢陰、洵陽、白河、竹山、竹溪、上津諸縣皆下。

translations.literal: Thereupon Pingli, Ziyang, Shiquan, Hanyin, Xunyang, Baihe, Zhushan, Zhuxi, Shangjin, and other counties all fell.
translations.idiomatic: Pingli, Ziyang, Shiquan, Hanyin, Xunyang, Baihe, Zhushan, Zhuxi, Shangjin, and the other counties then fell in turn.

sentences.zh: 興安既克，圖海統大軍之半屯鳳翔，尋移漢中，護諸軍餉。

translations.literal: Once Xing'an was taken, Tu Hai commanded half the main army stationed at Fengxiang, then moved to Hanzhong to oversee supplies for the armies.
translations.idiomatic: After Xing'an fell, Tu Hai kept half the main force at Fengxiang, then shifted his headquarters to Hanzhong to supervise army supplies.

sentences.zh: 會降將譚洪复叛，陝西總督哈佔溯江討之，詔圖海遙為聲援。

translations.literal: When the surrendered general Tan Hong rebelled again, Shaanxi Governor-General Hazhan pursued him upriver; an edict ordered Tu Hai to lend distant support.
translations.idiomatic: When the surrendered general Tan Hong rose again, Shaanxi Governor-General Hazhan pursued him up the river; Tu Hai was ordered to support the operation from a distance.

sentences.zh: 二十年，以疾徵還。

translations.literal: In the twentieth year he was recalled on account of illness.
translations.idiomatic: In Kangxi 20 illness brought him a recall to the capital.

sentences.zh: 卒，諡文襄。

translations.literal: He died and was given the posthumous title Wenxiang.
translations.idiomatic: He died and was posthumously titled Wenxiang.

sentences.zh: 太宗實錄成，贈少保兼太子太傅。

translations.literal: When the Veritable Records of Taizong were completed, he was posthumously given Junior Guardian and Grand Tutor of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: When the Veritable Records of Taizong were finished, he was posthumously made Junior Guardian and Grand Tutor of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 雍正初，追贈一等忠達公，配享太廟。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Yongzheng he was posthumously made first-rank Duke of Loyal Achievement and given joint sacrifice in the Imperial Ancestral Temple.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Yongzheng reign he was posthumously raised to first-rank Duke of Loyal Achievement and granted a place in the Imperial Ancestral Temple.

sentences.zh: 子諾敏，襲爵，歷刑、禮二部尚書，正黃旗蒙古都統。

translations.literal: His son Nuomin inherited the title, served as Minister of Justice and Minister of Rites, and as banner general of the Mongol Plain Yellow Banner.
translations.idiomatic: His son Nuomin inherited the title, held the ministries of Justice and Rites in turn, and became banner general of the Mongol Plain Yellow Banner.

sentences.zh: 諾敏子馬爾賽，自有傳。

translations.literal: Nuomin's son Ma'ersai has his own biography.
translations.idiomatic: Nuomin's son Ma'ersai is treated in a separate biography.

sentences.zh: 周昌初入城，自陳父明季死流寇，母孫剜目破面觸棺死，原捐軀表母烈。

translations.literal: When Zhou Chang first entered the city he declared that his father had died at the hands of bandits in the late Ming, and his mother Sun had gouged out her eyes, mutilated her face, and dashed herself against the coffin to die; he wished to give his life to manifest his mother's fidelity.
translations.idiomatic: On his first entry into the city Zhou Chang told how his father had been killed by late-Ming bandits and how his mother Sun had gouged out her eyes, scarred her face, and thrown herself against the coffin to die with her husband. He asked to give his own life to honor her devotion.

sentences.zh: 及輔臣降，圖海以聞。

translations.literal: When Fuchen surrendered, Tu Hai reported it to the throne.
translations.idiomatic: After Fuchen submitted, Tu Hai reported the matter to the throne.

sentences.zh: 上命旌其母，遣官致祭，授昌布政使參政。

translations.literal: The emperor ordered honors for his mother, dispatched officials to perform sacrifices, and appointed Chang provincial administration participation commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ordered honors for his mother, sent officials to perform the rites, and appointed Chang provincial administration participation commissioner.

sentences.zh: 昌复參蔡毓榮軍事，事平，授山東登萊道，攝布政使，以與總兵互訐罷。

translations.literal: Chang again took part in Cai Yurong's military affairs; when affairs were settled he was made Deng-Lai circuit intendant of Shandong and acted as provincial administration commissioner, but was dismissed for mutual accusations with the regional commander.
translations.idiomatic: Chang again served on Cai Yurong's staff. After the war he was made Deng-Lai circuit intendant in Shandong and acting provincial administration commissioner, but was dismissed after feuding with the regional commander.

sentences.zh: 昌既罷，猶喜言兵。

translations.literal: Though dismissed, Chang still delighted in discussing military affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Even after his dismissal Chang kept offering advice on military matters.

sentences.zh: 噶爾丹擾邊，數上書當事陳利害。

translations.literal: When Galdan harassed the frontier he repeatedly wrote to those in charge setting forth advantages and harms.
translations.idiomatic: When Galdan raided the frontier he wrote repeatedly to officials in charge, laying out the stakes.

sentences.zh: 後卒於家。

translations.literal: He later died at home.
translations.idiomatic: He later died at home.

sentences.zh: 李之芳，字鄴園，山東武定人。

translations.literal: Li Zhifang, styled Yeyuan, was a native of Wuding in Shandong.
translations.idiomatic: Li Zhifang, style Yeyuan, came from Wuding in Shandong.

sentences.zh: 順治四年進士，授金華府推官。

translations.literal: A jinshi of the fourth year of Shunzhi, he was appointed investigating censor of Jinhua Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi examination in Shunzhi 4 and was appointed investigating censor of Jinhua Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 卓異，擢刑部主事。

translations.literal: Rated outstanding, he was promoted to secretary in the Ministry of Justice.
translations.idiomatic: Marked outstanding in evaluation, he was promoted to secretary in the Ministry of Justice.

sentences.zh: 累遷郎中，授廣西道御史。

translations.literal: He rose through successive posts to director and was appointed censor of the Guangxi circuit.
translations.idiomatic: He rose through the ranks to director and was made censor of the Guangxi circuit.

sentences.zh: 疏請革錢糧陋規，禁州縣官迎送。

translations.literal: He memorialized asking to abolish corrupt practices in tax grain collection and to forbid prefectural and county officials from escorting visitors.
translations.idiomatic: He memorialized to abolish corrupt tax-collection practices and forbid prefectural and county officials from lavish escorts.

sentences.zh: 十七年，巡按山西。

translations.literal: In the seventeenth year he toured and inspected Shanxi.
translations.idiomatic: In Kangxi 17 he served as touring inspector of Shanxi.

sentences.zh: 聖祖即位，裁巡按，召回。

translations.literal: When the Sacred Ancestor took the throne the touring-inspector posts were abolished and he was recalled.
translations.idiomatic: When the Kangxi Emperor came to the throne the touring-inspector posts were abolished and Li was recalled.

sentences.zh: 康熙元年，乞假歸。

translations.literal: In the first year of Kangxi he asked leave and returned home.
translations.idiomatic: In Kangxi 1 he took leave and returned home.

sentences.zh: 二年，复授湖廣道御史。

translations.literal: In the second year he was again appointed censor of the Huguang circuit.
translations.idiomatic: In Kangxi 2 he was again made censor of the Huguang circuit.

sentences.zh: 五年，巡視浙江鹽政。

translations.literal: In the fifth year he inspected the salt administration of Zhejiang.
translations.idiomatic: In Kangxi 5 he inspected Zhejiang's salt administration.

sentences.zh: 入掌河南道事。

translations.literal: He entered charge of Henan circuit affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He took charge of Henan circuit affairs.

sentences.zh: 大學士班布爾善坐鰲拜黨誅，之芳疏言：「昔大學士俱內直，諸司章奏，即日票擬。

translations.literal: When Grand Secretary Banbu'ershan was executed for membership in Oboi's faction, Zhifang memorialized: "Formerly all grand secretaries served on internal duty, and memorials from the ministries received draft rescripts the same day."
translations.idiomatic: After Grand Secretary Banbu'ershan was executed as a member of Oboi's faction, Zhifang memorialized: "In former times every grand secretary kept internal duty, and ministry memorials received draft rescripts the same day."

sentences.zh: 自鰲拜輔政，大學士皆不入直，疏奏俱至次日看詳。

translations.literal: Since Oboi held regency the grand secretaries no longer kept internal duty, and all memorials were not reviewed until the next day.
translations.idiomatic: Once Oboi dominated the regency, grand secretaries no longer kept internal duty, and memorials were not reviewed until the following day.

sentences.zh: 請復舊制，杜任意更改之弊。

translations.literal: I ask that the old system be restored to stop the abuse of arbitrary alteration.
translations.idiomatic: Restore the old practice, he urged, to end the abuse of arbitrary tampering.

sentences.zh: 」又疏言：「世祖時賞罰出至公，督撫不敢恣睢無忌。

translations.literal: He also memorialized: "Under the Shizu Emperor rewards and punishments issued from utmost fairness, and governors-general and governors did not dare act lawlessly without restraint."
translations.idiomatic: He also wrote: "Under the Shizu Emperor rewards and punishments were utterly fair, and governors-general and governors did not dare run wild."

sentences.zh: 十八年以後，督撫率多夤緣而得，有恃無恐。

translations.literal: After the eighteenth year governors-general and governors mostly gained office through patronage and felt secure without fear.
translations.idiomatic: After Kangxi 18 most governors-general and governors won their posts through connections and acted without fear.

sentences.zh: 勒索屬員，擾害百姓。

translations.literal: They extorted subordinates and harassed the people.
translations.idiomatic: They squeezed their subordinates and preyed on the people.

sentences.zh: 夫直省億萬之眾，皆世祖留遺之群黎，我皇上愛養之赤子，何堪此輩朘削？

translations.literal: The hundreds of millions in the provinces are all the common people the Shizu Emperor left behind and the infants our emperor cherishes—how can they bear to be fleeced by such men?
translations.idiomatic: The tens of millions in the provinces are the people the Shizu Emperor bequeathed and the children our emperor nurtures—how can they endure being stripped by such men?

sentences.zh: 自與受同罪之法嚴，與者不承，則言者即涉虛，非特不敢糾督撫，且不敢糾司道守令。

translations.literal: Since the law punishing giver and taker alike became strict, if the taker does not confess the accuser is deemed false; not only do men not dare impeach governors-general and governors, they do not even dare impeach circuit intendants and prefects.
translations.idiomatic: With the law punishing briber and bribed alike, if the recipient denies guilt the accuser is treated as slanderous. Men no longer dare impeach governors-general and governors—nor even circuit intendants and magistrates.

sentences.zh: 有貪之利，無貪之害，又何憚而不怙惡自恣？

translations.literal: With the profit of corruption and no harm from it, why should they fear and not cling to evil and indulge themselves?
translations.idiomatic: When corruption pays and honesty costs, why should they shrink from clinging to evil and doing as they pleased?

sentences.zh: 今皇上親政，乞親裁，罷黜溺職督撫，以肅吏治。

translations.literal: Now that Your Majesty personally governs, I beg personal judgment to dismiss negligent governors-general and governors and rectify official discipline.
translations.idiomatic: Now that Your Majesty rules in person, I beg you to judge for yourself, dismiss negligent governors-general and governors, and restore official discipline.

sentences.zh: 」疏下部，尋甄別各省督撫，黜其尤者數人。

translations.literal: The memorial was sent to the ministries; soon governors-general and governors of each province were screened and several of the worst were dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: The memorial went to the ministries; soon the court screened provincial governors and dismissed several of the worst offenders.

sentences.zh: 進秩視四品，擢左副都御史。

translations.literal: His rank was advanced to equivalent fourth grade and he was promoted to Left Vice Censor-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: His rank was raised to equivalent fourth grade and he was made Left Vice Censor-in-Chief.

sentences.zh: 之芳數上封事，請嚴巡鹽考績，慎外官罰俸，皆關治體。

translations.literal: Zhifang repeatedly submitted sealed memorials asking for strict evaluation of salt inspectors, caution in fining outside officials, all matters bearing on the fundamentals of governance.
translations.idiomatic: Zhifang repeatedly submitted sealed memorials urging stricter evaluation of salt inspectors and caution in fining local officials—measures that touched the foundations of good government.

sentences.zh: 遷吏部侍郎。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Vice Minister of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to Vice Minister of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 十二年，以兵部侍郎總督浙江軍務。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year, as Vice Minister of War he was made governor-general of Zhejiang military affairs.
translations.idiomatic: In Kangxi 12, as Vice Minister of War, he was appointed to direct Zhejiang's military affairs.

sentences.zh: 會吳三桂反，十三年，奏請復標兵原額，督習槍砲。

translations.literal: When Wu Sangui rebelled, in the thirteenth year he memorialized to restore the original quota of banner troops and supervise drill in firearms and cannon.
translations.idiomatic: When Wu Sangui rebelled, in Kangxi 13 he asked to restore the Green Standard troops to full strength and supervised training in firearms and cannon.

sentences.zh: 疏甫上，耿精忠亦叛，遣其將曾養性、白顯忠、馬九玉數道闚浙，浙大震。

translations.literal: As soon as the memorial was submitted, Geng Jingzhong also rebelled and sent his generals Zeng Yangxing, Bai Xianzhong, and Ma Jiuyu in several columns to threaten Zhejiang; the whole province was shaken.
translations.idiomatic: Hardly had the memorial gone up when Geng Jingzhong rebelled too, sending Zeng Yangxing, Bai Xianzhong, and Ma Jiuyu against Zhejiang by several routes. The province was thrown into alarm.

sentences.zh: 之芳檄諸將扼仙霞關，調總兵李榮率副將王廷梅、牟大寅、陳世凱、鮑虎等分道禦寇。

translations.literal: Zhifang ordered the generals to hold Xianxia Pass and summoned Regional Commander Li Rong with deputy commanders Wang Tingmei, Mou Dayin, Chen Shikai, Bao Hu, and others to resist the enemy on separate routes.
translations.idiomatic: Zhifang ordered his generals to hold Xianxia Pass and called up Regional Commander Li Rong with deputies Wang Tingmei, Mou Dayin, Chen Shikai, Bao Hu, and others to meet the invaders on several fronts.

sentences.zh: 時上命都統賴塔率師入浙，五月，偕賴塔率滿洲兵千、綠旗兵二千、鄉勇五百，進駐衢州。

translations.literal: At that time the emperor ordered Banner Commander Laita to lead troops into Zhejiang; in the fifth month Zhifang joined Laita leading one thousand Manchu troops, two thousand Green Standard troops, and five hundred militia, and advanced to garrison Quzhou.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor had ordered Banner Commander Laita into Zhejiang. In the fifth month Zhifang joined him with one thousand Manchu troops, two thousand Green Standard soldiers, and five hundred militia, and marched into Quzhou.

sentences.zh: 眾皆謂會城重地，不宜輕委。

translations.literal: All said the provincial capital was a vital place and should not be lightly entrusted elsewhere.
translations.idiomatic: Everyone said the provincial capital was too important to leave lightly defended.

sentences.zh: 之芳曰：「不然。

translations.literal: Zhifang said: "That is not so."
translations.idiomatic: Zhifang said, "Not so."

sentences.zh: 衢踞上游，無衢，是無浙也。

translations.literal: Quzhou sits on the upper reaches; without Quzhou there is no Zhejiang.
translations.idiomatic: Quzhou commands the upper river—lose Quzhou and you lose Zhejiang.

sentences.zh: 今日之事，義無反顧。

translations.literal: In today's affair there is no turning back on duty.
translations.idiomatic: Today's fight brooks no retreat.

sentences.zh: 」顯忠自常山陷開化、壽昌、淳安，養性自處州犯義烏、浦江、東陽、湯溪，沿河阻餉道。

translations.literal: Xianzhong from Changshan took Kaihua, Shouchang, and Chun'an; Yangxing from Chuzhou attacked Yiwu, Pujiang, Dongyang, and Tangxi, blocking the supply route along the river.
translations.idiomatic: Xianzhong swept from Changshan into Kaihua, Shouchang, and Chun'an; Yangxing advanced from Chuzhou against Yiwu, Pujiang, Dongyang, and Tangxi, cutting the river supply line.

sentences.zh: 溫州鎮總兵祖弘勳叛，召寇陷平陽，再進陷黃岩，集悍卒數万窺衢州。

translations.literal: The Wenzhou garrison regional commander Zu Hongxun rebelled, summoned the enemy to take Pingyang, advanced again to take Huangyan, and gathered tens of thousands of fierce troops to threaten Quzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Wenzhou garrison commander Zu Hongxun rebelled, called in rebels to seize Pingyang, pushed on to Huangyan, and massed tens of thousands of hardened troops against Quzhou.

sentences.zh: 七月，之芳與賴塔閱兵水亭門，率總兵官李榮、副都統瑚圖等薄賊壘，軍坑西。

translations.literal: In the seventh month Zhifang and Laita reviewed troops at the Water Pavilion Gate, led Regional Commander Li Rong, Vice Banner Commander Hutu, and others to press the rebel camp, and encamped west of Junkeng.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month Zhifang and Laita reviewed the troops at Water Pavilion Gate, then led Li Rong, Hutu, and others against the rebel camp and encamped west of Junkeng.

sentences.zh: 之芳手執刀督陣，或請少避，之芳曰：「三軍司命在吾，退即為賊乘。

translations.literal: Zhifang personally held a blade to direct the battle line; when some asked him to withdraw a little he said: "The fate of the three armies rests on me; if I retreat the enemy will seize the advantage."
translations.idiomatic: Zhifang took a blade in hand to direct the line. When aides urged him to step back he said, "The army's fate rests on me—retreat and the enemy will overrun us."

sentences.zh: 今日勝敗，即吾死生矣！

translations.literal: Today's victory or defeat is my life or death!
translations.idiomatic: Victory or defeat today is my life or death!

sentences.zh: 」守備程龍怯戰，斬以徇。

translations.literal: The garrison commander Cheng Long showed cowardice in battle and was beheaded as an example.
translations.idiomatic: Garrison commander Cheng Long had hung back in the fight; Zhifang beheaded him as an example to the ranks.

sentences.zh: 麾眾越壕拔柵，敗之。

translations.literal: He commanded the troops over the moat to tear down the palisade and defeated them.
translations.idiomatic: He led his men over the ditch, tore down the palisade, and routed the enemy.

sentences.zh: 遣陳世凱乘勝复義烏、湯​​溪，鮑虎复壽昌、淳安，牟大寅破常山，王廷梅敗賊於金華石梁、大溝源，李榮亦復東陽，复敗賊於金華壽溪，馘賊將，毀寨十八。

translations.literal: He sent Chen Shikai to follow up the victory and recover Yiwu and Tangxi, Bao Hu to recover Shouchang and Chun'an, Mou Dayin to break Changshan, Wang Tingmei to defeat the enemy at Jinhua Shiliang and Dagouyuan; Li Rong also recovered Dongyang and again defeated the enemy at Jinhua Shouxi, beheading a rebel general and destroying eighteen stockades.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Shikai pressed the victory to retake Yiwu and Tangxi; Bao Hu retook Shouchang and Chun'an; Mou Dayin broke Changshan; Wang Tingmei routed the enemy at Jinhua Shiliang and Dagouyuan; Li Rong recovered Dongyang and won again at Jinhua Shouxi, beheading a rebel general and destroying eighteen camps.

sentences.zh: 參將洪起元復嵊縣。

translations.literal: Assistant Regional Commander Hong Qiyuan recovered Sheng County.
translations.idiomatic: Assistant Regional Commander Hong Qiyuan retook Sheng County.

sentences.zh: 詔嘉之芳調度有方。

translations.literal: An edict praised Zhifang's well-ordered command.
translations.idiomatic: An edict commended Zhifang's skillful command.

sentences.zh: 十月，賊將桑明等五萬眾由常山逼衢州西溝溪，倚山為營，覬聯南路賊巢。

translations.literal: In the tenth month the rebel generals Sang Ming and others with fifty thousand men pressed from Changshan on Xigouxi west of Quzhou, camped against the mountains, and hoped to link with rebel nests on the southern route.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month rebel generals led by Sang Ming—fifty thousand strong—advanced from Changshan on Xigouxi west of Quzhou, entrenched along the hills, and tried to link up with rebel strongholds to the south.

sentences.zh: 之芳與賴塔議，出不意，遣廷梅與參領禪布夜趨溝溪，分隊進攻，又大破之，賊棄營遁。

translations.literal: Zhifang and Laita planned a surprise move, sent Tingmei and company commander Chanbu by night to rush on Gouxi, attacked in separate columns, again routed them utterly, and the rebels abandoned camp and fled.
translations.idiomatic: Zhifang and Laita planned a surprise: Wang Tingmei and company commander Chanbu marched on Gouxi by night, attacked in columns, broke the enemy again, and the rebels abandoned camp and fled.

sentences.zh: 十四年，康親王杰書破曾養性金華，复處州；

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year Prince Kang Jieshu broke Zeng Yangxing at Jinhua and recovered Chuzhou;
translations.idiomatic: In Kangxi 14 Prince Kang Jieshu defeated Zeng Yangxing at Jinhua and retook Chuzhou;

sentences.zh: 貝子傅拉塔亦復黃岩，進圍溫州。

translations.literal: Prince Fu'lata also recovered Huangyan and advanced to besiege Wenzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Fu'lata also retook Huangyan and moved to besiege Wenzhou.

sentences.zh: 惟九玉踞江山、常山、開化，連寨數十，與之芳相持。

translations.literal: Only Jiuyu held Jiangshan, Changshan, and Kaihua with several tens of linked stockades, locked in stalemate with Zhifang.
translations.idiomatic: Only Ma Jiuyu still held Jiangshan, Changshan, and Kaihua behind dozens of linked camps, deadlocked with Zhifang.

sentences.zh: 五月，乘大雨河溢，由南塘搗賊前嶺，陣斬七百餘級。

translations.literal: In the fifth month, taking advantage of heavy rain and flooded rivers, he struck from Nantang at the rebels' forward ridge and slew more than seven hundred in the field.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month, using heavy rains and flooded rivers as cover, he struck from Nantang at the rebels' forward ridge and killed more than seven hundred in battle.

sentences.zh: 十五年，遣將自遂安連破賊寨，遂復開化。

translations.literal: In the fifteenth year he sent generals from Suian to break rebel stockades in succession and thus recovered Kaihua.
translations.idiomatic: In Kangxi 15 he sent generals from Suian to smash rebel camps one after another and retook Kaihua.

sentences.zh: 會鄭錦入漳、泉，耿繼祚方攻建昌潰營遁。

translations.literal: When Zheng Jing entered Zhang and Quan, Geng Jizuo had just attacked Jianchang, his camp collapsed, and he fled.
translations.idiomatic: When Zheng Jing invaded Zhang and Quan, Geng Jizuo had been attacking Jianchang; his force collapsed and he fled.

sentences.zh: 上知閩中有變，命王撤溫州之圍取福建，之芳乃建議直搗仙霞關，曰：「進取之路，不在溫、處而在衢。

translations.literal: Learning of trouble in Fujian, the emperor ordered the prince to lift the siege of Wenzhou and take Fujian; Zhifang then proposed striking straight at Xianxia Pass, saying: "The route of advance lies not in Wen and Chu but in Qu."
translations.idiomatic: When word came of trouble in Fujian, the emperor ordered the prince to abandon the siege of Wenzhou and march on Fujian. Zhifang urged a direct strike at Xianxia Pass: "The road forward lies not through Wenzhou or Chuzhou but through Quzhou."

sentences.zh: 雖九玉死守河西難猝破，然其南江山，西則常山，皆間道可襲。

translations.literal: Though Jiuyu stubbornly defends the west of the river and cannot quickly be broken, yet south of him lies Jiangshan and west lies Changshan—both side routes that can be struck.
translations.idiomatic: Jiuyu may hold the west bank stubbornly, but Jiangshan lies to his south and Changshan to his west—both are paths we can strike along.

sentences.zh: 我兵一進，使彼首尾受敵，即河西之壘不能獨完。

translations.literal: Once our troops advance and make him attacked at head and tail, even the west-bank fort cannot stand alone intact.
translations.idiomatic: Once our troops move, he will be caught front and rear, and even his west-bank stronghold cannot hold alone.

sentences.zh: 」王至衢州，從之芳議。

translations.literal: When the prince reached Quzhou he followed Zhifang's plan.
translations.idiomatic: When the prince reached Quzhou he adopted Zhifang's plan.

sentences.zh: 遂進兵大溪灘，复江山，九玉走，欲別取道奪仙霞。

translations.literal: He then advanced to Daxitan, recovered Jiangshan; Jiuyu fled and wished to take another route to seize Xianxia.
translations.idiomatic: The army advanced to Daxitan and retook Jiangshan. Jiuyu fled and tried to seize Xianxia by another route.

sentences.zh: 諸將受之芳密檄，急據關夾擊，其將金應虎等窮蹙降。

translations.literal: The generals received Zhifang's secret dispatch, swiftly held the pass and attacked from both sides; his generals Jin Yinghu and others, driven to extremity, surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: On Zhifang's secret orders the generals seized the pass and attacked from both sides; Jin Yinghu and other rebel commanders, cornered, surrendered.

sentences.zh: 王師下福建，臨行，之芳啟曰：「王但飭諸軍勿虜掠，即長驅入，兵可不血刃也。

translations.literal: As the imperial army descended on Fujian, on the eve of departure Zhifang reported: "If Your Highness only orders the armies not to plunder, you may drive straight in and the troops need not stain their blades."
translations.idiomatic: As the imperial army prepared to enter Fujian, Zhifang advised the prince: "Order your men not to loot, march straight in, and you may take the province without drawing a sword."

sentences.zh: 」未幾精忠降，溫、處賊皆潰散。

translations.literal: Before long Jingzhong surrendered and the rebels in Wen and Chu all collapsed and scattered.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Jingzhong surrendered and the rebel forces in Wenzhou and Chuzhou melted away.

sentences.zh: 精忠所署置總兵馬鵬、汪文生、陳山，將軍程鳳等猶踞玉山、鉛山、弋陽、德興，之芳請會剿。

translations.literal: Jingzhong's appointed regional commanders Ma Peng, Wang Wensheng, and Chen Shan, and General Cheng Feng, still held Yushan, Qianshan, Yiyang, and Dexing; Zhifang asked for a joint suppression.
translations.idiomatic: Jingzhong's appointees Ma Peng, Wang Wensheng, Chen Shan, and General Cheng Feng still held Yushan, Qianshan, Yiyang, and Dexing; Zhifang requested a joint campaign against them.

sentences.zh: 時吳三桂兵寇吉安、袁州，江西兵不能東，乃獨遣兵复玉山，文生遁；

translations.literal: At that time Wu Sangui's troops were raiding Ji'an and Yuanzhou and Jiangxi troops could not move east; he therefore sent troops alone to recover Yushan, and Wensheng fled;
translations.idiomatic: Wu Sangui's forces were threatening Ji'an and Yuanzhou, so Jiangxi troops could not march east. Zhifang sent his own force to retake Yushan, and Wensheng fled;

sentences.zh: 自白沙關趨德興，擒鵬；

translations.literal: from Baisha Pass he pressed on Dexing and captured Peng;
translations.idiomatic: pressed from Baisha Pass into Dexing and captured Peng;

sentences.zh: 遣游擊郭守金等復鉛山、興安、弋陽、貴溪諸縣。

translations.literal: he dispatched Brigadier Guo Shoujin and others to recover Qianshan, Xing'an, Yiyang, Guixi, and other counties.
translations.idiomatic: and sent Brigadier Guo Shoujin and others to retake Qianshan, Xing'an, Yiyang, Guixi, and the other counties.

sentences.zh: 上嘉之芳勦賊鄰省有功，加兵部尚書銜。

translations.literal: The emperor commended Zhifang's merit in suppressing rebels in a neighboring province and gave him the nominal rank of Minister of War.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor praised Zhifang's success against rebels in a neighboring province and granted him the nominal rank of Minister of War.

sentences.zh: 十六年，遣參將蔣懋勳等敗賊玉山椒岩，山降。

translations.literal: In the sixteenth year he sent Assistant Regional Commander Jiang Maoxun and others to defeat the rebels at Yushan Jiaoyan; Chen Shan surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: In Kangxi 16 he sent Assistant Regional Commander Jiang Maoxun and others to rout the rebels at Yushan Jiaoyan, and Chen Shan submitted.

sentences.zh: 先是文生、鳳皆乞降，而鳳病死，其妻王玉貞籍所屬六萬八千餘人就撫，而精忠將林爾瞻猶擁眾石壟。

translations.literal: Earlier Wensheng and Feng had both begged to surrender; Feng died of illness, and his wife Wang Yuzhen registered more than sixty-eight thousand followers for pacification, but Jingzhong's general Lin Erzhan still held a crowd at Shilong.
translations.idiomatic: Wensheng and Feng had already offered to surrender; Feng died of illness, and his wife Wang Yuzhen registered more than sixty-eight thousand followers for pacification. Yet Jingzhong's general Lin Erzhan still held out at Shilong with a large force.

sentences.zh: 之芳令懋勳等扼要隘，自以數十騎入寨，往撫慰之，爾瞻乃降。

translations.literal: Zhifang ordered Maoxun and others to hold the key passes, himself entered the stockade with several tens of horsemen to console them, and Erzhan then surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: Zhifang had Maoxun seal the key passes, then rode into the camp with only a few dozen men to reassure them—and Erzhan surrendered.

sentences.zh: 十七年，擊賊子午口，克八仙、老鼠諸洞，賊寨悉平。

translations.literal: In the seventeenth year he attacked the rebels at Ziwukou, took the caves of Baxian and Laoshu, and all rebel stockades were pacified.
translations.idiomatic: In Kangxi 17 he struck the rebels at Ziwukou, took the Baxian and Laoshu cave strongholds, and cleared every rebel camp.

sentences.zh: 鄭錦寇瀕海，遣將嚴守禦，敗之於廟嶺湖，又敗之於溫州。

translations.literal: When Zheng Jing raided the coast he sent generals to guard strictly, defeated him at Miaoling Lake, and defeated him again at Wenzhou.
translations.idiomatic: When Zheng Jing raided the coast Zhifang posted defenders, beat him at Miaoling Lake, and beat him again off Wenzhou.

sentences.zh: 錦將詹天樞詣世凱降。

translations.literal: Jing's general Zhan Tianshu went to Chen Shikai to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng's general Zhan Tianshu came to Chen Shikai and surrendered.

sentences.zh: 十八年，檄定海總兵牟大寅斬錦將童耀等孝順洋，奪獲船隻、器械以還。

translations.literal: In the eighteenth year he ordered Dinghai regional commander Mou Dayin to behead Jing's general Tong Yao and others at Xiaoshunyang, seizing ships and weapons and returning.
translations.idiomatic: In Kangxi 18 he ordered Dinghai commander Mou Dayin to destroy Zheng's general Tong Yao and others at Xiaoshunyang, capturing their ships and arms.

sentences.zh: 之芳練世故，沉幾善謀。

translations.literal: Zhifang was seasoned in worldly affairs, deep in counsel and skilled in planning.
translations.idiomatic: Zhifang knew the ways of the world, kept his own counsel, and planned with care.

sentences.zh: 康親王師將行，問之芳：「所策固萬全乎？

translations.literal: When Prince Kang's army was about to march he asked Zhifang: "Is the plan truly foolproof?"
translations.idiomatic: Before Prince Kang's army marched, he asked Zhifang, "Is your plan truly foolproof?"

sentences.zh: 」之芳曰：「軍已發，猶豫則士氣沮。

translations.literal: Zhifang said: "The army has already set out; hesitation will damp morale."
translations.idiomatic: Zhifang replied, "The army is already on the march—hesitation will kill its spirit."

sentences.zh: 」乃詣王曰：「虜在吾目中久，明日捷書至矣！

translations.literal: He then went to the prince and said: "The enemy has long been within my sight; tomorrow the victory dispatch will arrive!"
translations.idiomatic: He then told the prince, "I have had these rebels in my sights for some time—tomorrow the victory report will arrive!"

sentences.zh: 」前軍捷書果至，傑書大喜，以為神。

translations.literal: The vanguard victory report indeed arrived; Jieshu was greatly pleased and regarded it as miraculous.
translations.idiomatic: The victory report from the vanguard did arrive the next day; Jieshu was delighted and took it for prophecy.

sentences.zh: 在杭州，與將軍圖喇約為兄弟。

translations.literal: At Hangzhou he pledged brotherhood with General Tula.
translations.idiomatic: At Hangzhou he swore brotherhood with General Tula.

sentences.zh: 精忠既叛，語圖喇勿縱兵暴民。

translations.literal: When Jingzhong rebelled he told Tula not to let the troops brutalize the people.
translations.idiomatic: When Jingzhong rebelled he urged Tula not to let his soldiers terrorize the populace.

sentences.zh: 有滿兵犯法，之芳縛詣圖喇，以軍法治之，一軍肅然。

translations.literal: When a Manchu soldier broke the law Zhifang bound him and brought him before Tula to be punished by military law; the whole army was awed into order.
translations.idiomatic: When a Manchu soldier broke the law Zhifang bound him and brought him before Tula for military punishment—and the whole army fell into line.

sentences.zh: 浙亂平，疏請蠲被兵州縣額賦，安輯流亡，甚有威惠。

translations.literal: When the Zhejiang rebellion was pacified he memorialized to remit the assessed taxes of counties ravaged by war and to settle displaced persons, winning great authority and kindness.
translations.idiomatic: After the Zhejiang rebellion ended he asked to remit taxes in war-ravaged counties and resettle refugees, earning wide respect and gratitude.

sentences.zh: 所拔偏裨，皆累功至方鎮，而之芳以督臣不敘。

translations.literal: The subordinate officers he promoted all rose through accumulated merit to frontier commands, yet Zhifang as governor did not enter his own merits in the record.
translations.idiomatic: The officers he promoted all rose on merit to high frontier commands, yet Zhifang as governor never entered his own name for reward.

sentences.zh: 久之，追論大溪灘破賊功，授拖沙喇哈番，準襲一次。

translations.literal: After a long while his merit in defeating the enemy at Daxitan was reviewed posthumously and he was granted Tushala Banner rank with permission for one inheritance.
translations.idiomatic: Long afterward the court reviewed his victory at Daxitan and granted him Tushala Banner rank, inheritable once.

sentences.zh: 入為兵部尚書，調吏部。

translations.literal: He entered the capital as Minister of War and was transferred to the Ministry of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: He entered the capital as Minister of War and was then moved to the Ministry of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 二十六年，授文華殿大學士。

translations.literal: In the twenty-sixth year he was appointed Grand Secretary of the Hall of Literary Splendor.
translations.idiomatic: In Kangxi 26 he was made Grand Secretary of the Hall of Literary Splendor.

sentences.zh: 二十七年，御史郭琇疏劾大學士明珠，謂內閣票擬，皆聽明珠指揮，上既罷明珠，並命之芳休致。

translations.literal: In the twenty-seventh year Censor Guo Xiu memorialized to impeach Grand Secretary Mingzhu, saying that draft rescripts in the Grand Secretariat all followed Mingzhu's direction; the emperor dismissed Mingzhu and also ordered Zhifang to retire.
translations.idiomatic: In Kangxi 27 Censor Guo Xiu impeached Grand Secretary Mingzhu, charging that every Grand Secretariat draft followed Mingzhu's orders. The emperor dismissed Mingzhu and ordered Zhifang to retire as well.

sentences.zh: 三十三年，卒於家，諡文襄。

translations.literal: In the thirty-third year he died at home and was given the posthumous title Wenxiang.
translations.idiomatic: In Kangxi 33 he died at home and was posthumously titled Wenxiang.

sentences.zh: 之芳既卒，聖祖思其功，嘗諭群臣曰：「人能效命，即為勇士。

translations.literal: After Zhifang died the Sacred Ancestor recalled his merit and once told the ministers: "A man who can give his life in duty is a brave warrior."
translations.idiomatic: After Zhifang's death the Kangxi Emperor remembered his service and once told the ministers, "A man who gives his life for duty is a true warrior."

sentences.zh: 耿精忠叛，時之芳為總督，雖不諳騎射，執刀立船首，率眾突前破敵。

translations.literal: When Geng Jingzhong rebelled Zhifang was governor; though not skilled in riding and archery, he held a blade standing at the bow and led the troops in a forward rush to break the enemy.
translations.idiomatic: When Geng Jingzhong rebelled, Zhifang was governor. Though no horseman or archer, he stood at the prow with a blade in hand and led a charge that broke the enemy.

sentences.zh: 彼時同出征者，還京皆稱其勇。

translations.literal: Those who campaigned with him at that time, on returning to the capital, all praised his courage.
translations.idiomatic: Every comrade on that campaign praised his courage when they returned to the capital.

sentences.zh: 今承平久，善射，能約束士卒，尚不乏人。

translations.literal: Now that peace has long endured, men skilled in archery who can restrain troops are still not lacking.
translations.idiomatic: In these long years of peace we still have plenty of good archers who can keep their men in order.

sentences.zh: 若屢經戰陣者，甚難得也！

translations.literal: But men who have repeatedly seen battle are very hard to find!
translations.idiomatic: Men who have seen battle again and again are very hard to find!

sentences.zh: 」世宗命立賢良祠，諭曰：「德若湯斌、功若之芳者，祀之。

translations.literal: The Shizong Emperor ordered the Hall of Worthies established and instructed: "Honor men of virtue like Tang Bin and of merit like Zhifang."
translations.idiomatic: The Yongzheng Emperor ordered the Hall of Worthies built with the instruction: "Enshrine men of Tang Bin's virtue and Zhifang's achievement."

sentences.zh: 」乾隆間，錄勳臣後，命予恩騎尉，世襲。

translations.literal: In the Qianlong period, when recording the descendants of meritorious ministers, his line was granted the Enlisted Cavalry Commandant rank with hereditary succession.
translations.idiomatic: Under Qianlong, when the court registered descendants of meritorious ministers, his line was granted the Enlisted Cavalry Commandant rank as an inheritable title.

sentences.zh: 論曰：圖海始阻撤籓之議，及其鷹揚西土，綏靖秦隴，卒收底川之績。

translations.literal: The commentator says: Tu Hai at first opposed the proposal to remove the princely fiefs; later he soared in the west, pacified Qin and Long, and in the end reaped the achievement of settling the rivers.
translations.idiomatic: The historian writes: Tu Hai first opposed removing the princely fiefs; then he took the field in the west, pacified Qin and Long, and at last won the credit for finishing the war on the rivers.

sentences.zh: 川軍入滇，遂竟全功。

translations.literal: When the Sichuan army entered Yunnan, the whole task was at last completed.
translations.idiomatic: Once the Sichuan army entered Yunnan, the great enterprise was complete.

sentences.zh: 之芳力扼三衢，敵雖東略，終不能得志仙霞。

translations.literal: Zhifang strove to hold the three Qu prefectures; though the enemy thrust eastward, they could never gain their aim at Xianxia.
translations.idiomatic: Zhifang held the three Qu prefectures firm; though the enemy pushed east, they never took Xianxia Pass.

sentences.zh: 下閩之功，與有勞焉。

translations.literal: In the merit of descending on Fujian he shared the labor.
translations.idiomatic: He shared in the merit of the conquest of Fujian.

sentences.zh: 雖曰遭時盤錯，抑亦聖祖馭材之效哉？

translations.literal: Though one may say they met a tangled age, was it not also the effect of the Sacred Ancestor's mastery in employing talent?
translations.idiomatic: They lived in troubled times, no doubt—but was that not also proof of the Kangxi Emperor's gift for using men?

sentences.zh: 並踐綸輔，易名曰襄。

translations.literal: Both reached the rank of grand minister and were given the same posthumous name Xiang.
translations.idiomatic: Both rose to the highest ministerial rank and share the posthumous name Xiang.

sentences.zh: 嗚呼，偉矣！

translations.literal: Alas, how great they were!
translations.idiomatic: Alas—how great they were!
